title: Why he did not ask Bouveau for a ticket home
summary: Nierenberg presses why he stayed four years; Bubbles says the Consulate had made him its responsibility and he waited on it.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: But you wouldn't work for Lee Bouveau.
No.
But you stayed there for four years.
Yeah.
Couldn't he have just given you a ticket home, Mr. Bouveau?
He didn't.
Did you ask him?
No.
Did you want to do that? You didn't want him to send you back home?
Listen, I wanted to get a ticket back but I'm not asking him because the American Consulate took over the point which was most interesting to me. Whatever the American Consulate said, that's what
would be done because the American Consultate made me his responsibility until I arrived back into America. So I ain't got nothin' to worry about. Understand?
What authority did the American Consulate have over him?
All these possibilities, to stop everything he was doing over there, that's what they did to him.
He wasn't American, was he?
No, -- oh, yeah, yeah.
Oh, he was American.
Yeah.
So now you're being taken care of by Leo Bouveau.
That's right.
But the first place he gets me at the Hauserzuhoff Hotel, he don't probably have to pay for that because the office which I was booked out of

to Kaiserslautern, they already okayed my expenses for that room at the time they told her to let me come, Lee had taken my bags to go and do the date. So whether he paid anything, I don't know. But he hadn't paid nothing where I'm concerned. The last thing he paid for was the telegram, I guess. I don't know, I don't think he sent the telegram. I think the company sent it. He might have sent it for them.
The telegram to whom?
To me to come.
So really Le Bouveau was getting off pretty easy.
Yeah, got off.
And he was not required to send you back to the states. In other words you didn't ask the American Consulate to instruct him to send you back to the states. Didn't you want to go back to the states?
Yeah, but I didn't ask him.
But you didn't have the money.
No.
And you just didn't want to ask, right?

I was just waiting to see what the American Consultate was going to do. The Consulate was there, it's in his hands. I don't want the police to arrest, the police don't know whether to arrest him or not. I don't have to ask the American Consulate what's to be done. They know that I live in America. They know that. They didn't ask me did I want to go to America. They didn't ask me that question. "Are you trying to get back home? They didn't ask me that question. I just told them the situation of what happened.
